title: Electricity cost history, 1980–2035
provenance: User-supplied sourcebook in this editing session; CSV blocks extracted verbatim, without rounding, recalculation or evidence-flag changes.
verification_status: Raw supplied data; not independently verified as a whole. Downstream plots must record their checked sources and distinguish benchmark, model and scenario data.
licensing: Numerical facts retain their cited source provenance. This snapshot does not assert that provider tables or prose share the repository content licence.

units.annual_electricity: constant 2025 US cents per kWh of electricity
units.PV_capex: 2025 USD per W or kW of installed PV power, as specified
units.storage_capex: 2025 USD per kWh of storage energy capacity, as specified

evidence_flags.B: published benchmark, occasionally rounded or digitised
evidence_flags.P: fuel-cost proxy, not a generating-plant LCOE

interpretation.comparability: IRENA global new-project renewables, US Lazard new-build conventional plants, synthetic daily storage and selected-site Nevada dispatch are different geographical and methodological populations.
interpretation.daily_storage: 60% of delivered electricity shifted through battery; not firm supply or seasonal storage.
interpretation.annual_95pct: 95% of annual demand energy, not 95% of hours fully served or guaranteed reliability.
interpretation.historical_backcasts: Pre-2010 solar generation costs and many early conventional/renewable points are reconstructions.
interpretation.oil_proxy: Exclude from full LCOE comparison unless explicitly labelled as a fuel proxy.
interpretation.capital_vs_energy: Do not place USD/W PV or USD/kWh battery-capacity costs on the electricity-LCOE axis.
interpretation.projections: 2030 and 2035 values are scenarios, not observations.
